milestone_brief:
corpus-integrity-observability-m3 — LanceDB unindexed-rows guard (scout CAND-10)

The on-theme leftover from the 2026q2-observability-reporting scout. Read its disposition
first: .claude/notes/capability-scouts/2026q2-observability-reporting/artifacts/challenge.md
(CAND-10, ~line 398) — MINOR, scope-adjusted to the v0 below.

PROBLEM (same silent-divergence bug class the e1/e2/e3 work killed). The LanceDB chunks
table carries two HNSW ANN indexes (on embedding_stmt + embedding_proof). If rows are
committed but the ANN index is NOT rebuilt to cover them, the ANN query silently falls
back to BRUTE-FORCE over the unindexed rows — correct results, but a silent performance
degradation that NOTHING surfaces. Today ingest/store.py::_create_indices runs
SYNCHRONOUSLY inside write_chunks (the index is built before write_chunks returns), so in
normal operation num_unindexed_rows == 0. That makes this guard a PURE TRIPWIRE: any
non-zero value is ALWAYS abnormal (corruption, a partial write, or a future async-index
path). The operator-facing message must say so.

FIX (mirror m2's startup-reconciliation shape almost exactly — Resources.startup_chunk_count
+ the arxmcp_corpus_chunk_count_* gauges + refresh_metrics_from_singleton_state, all
shipped in corpus-integrity-observability-m2). At Resources.startup, after the LanceDB
table is open (and after the m2 count_rows block), compute the total num_unindexed_rows
ONCE, cache it on a new Resources field (e.g. startup_unindexed_rows: int = -1 sentinel),
and expose it as a scalar Prometheus gauge arxmcp_corpus_unindexed_rows set once from the
cached value in refresh_metrics_from_singleton_state (NEVER recomputed per /metrics scrape
— same contract as the m2 gauges). On a non-zero count: WARN log naming the count + the
per-index breakdown.

ROBUSTNESS (challenge Axis 8). Do NOT hardcode index names. Discover the active ANN index
names via tbl.list_indices() (confirm the lancedb 0.30.x API name — it may be
list_indices() / list_indexes()), then call tbl.index_stats(index_name) for each and sum
num_unindexed_rows. Wrap the WHOLE thing in try/except: on unknown/unavailable index API
or any error, log a WARN and set the cached value to the -1 sentinel (gauge reports -1.0
= "unavailable"), and NEVER fail startup (FM-2 style, exactly like m2's count_rows guard).
The reconciliation must run only on the happy path (mirror m2 FM-7: if degraded is already
set by the corpus_corruption fallback, skip — do not clobber).

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION for research to resolve (cite m2's degraded precedent): should a
non-zero unindexed-rows count flip /readyz to degraded (reason="unindexed_rows"), or is
WARN + gauge sufficient? Lean: WARN + gauge ONLY, NOT degraded — brute-force ANN still
serves CORRECT results (just slower), so it is not a correctness degradation the way
chunk_count divergence / corpus_corruption is. But research should weigh this against the
"non-zero is always abnormal" framing and recommend.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Given a corpus with unindexed rows (simulate via a stubbed index_stats or a real
  partial-index fixture), when the server starts, then it logs a WARN naming the count
  and a non-zero arxmcp_corpus_unindexed_rows gauge is exposed.
- Given a fully-indexed corpus (num_unindexed_rows == 0), when the server starts, then no
  WARN and the gauge is 0.
- Given index_stats()/list_indices() unavailable or raising, when the server starts, then
  it does NOT crash — the cached value is the -1 sentinel, the gauge reports -1.0, a WARN
  is logged, and /readyz still reaches 200.
- The gauge is set once at startup from a single cached value; a test asserts index_stats
  is NOT called per /metrics scrape (mirror the m2 count_rows-once test).
- EXPECTED_TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256 + EXPECTED_BP1_SHA256 UNCHANGED (no MCP tool surface change);
  no CHUNKER_VERSION bump; make test green.

CONSTRAINTS: local-first; no new dependency; assert BANNED for invariants in server/+ingest/
(use if ... raise / WARN-and-continue); pure-ASGI only (n/a). Mirror the m2 pattern verbatim
(Resources cached field + gauge in refresh_metrics_from_singleton_state + getattr-defended
reads + the degraded zero-out enumeration if a new reason is added). Likely files:
server/resources.py (startup + cached field), server/health.py or server/metrics.py (the
gauge + reader), tests; possibly server/config.py only if a toggle is wanted (probably not).
Regenerate tests/fixtures/metrics_sample.txt if a new gauge family is added (this bit e2/e3).

External writes: none expected (purely local).

research_briefs.summary: mirror m2; gauge in health.py; lancedb 0.30.2 list_indices+index_stats verified
WARN+gauge not degraded; no-index must be -1 not 0; fixture regen mandatory
